facts.statement: The genus Qantassaurus was described by Rich and Vickers-Rich in 1999.
facts.quote: authority: Rich & Vickers-Rich, 1999

facts.statement: Qantassaurus lived in Australia approximately 125 to 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: lived in Australia about 125-112 million years ago

facts.statement: Qantassaurus was a basal, two-legged, plant-eating ornithischian dinosaur belonging to the clade Elasmaria.
facts.quote: basal two-legged, plant-eating elasmarian ornithischian dinosaur

facts.statement: The dinosaur was named after the Australian airline Qantas.
facts.quote: named after Qantas, the Australian airline

facts.statement: Qantassaurus was approximately 1.8 meters long and one meter high.
facts.quote: Qantassaurus was probably about 1.8 meters (6 feet) long, and about one meter (3 feet) high

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Qantassaurus was likely a fast runner.
facts.quote: probably was a fast runner

facts.statement: Qantassaurus had feet with claws for traction and a long tail stiffened by ossified tendons that likely aided in turning.
facts.quote: Its feet had claws for traction, and a long tail probably helped with turning, stiffened by ossified tendons

facts.statement: Qantassaurus possessed ten teeth in each lower jaw.
facts.quote: It had ten teeth in each lower jaw

facts.statement: Qantassaurus likely had a beak and leaf-shaped cheek teeth that were shed and replaced as they wore down.
facts.quote: It probably had a beak, and possessed leaf-shaped teeth back in its cheek, which were shed as they wore down, and replaced by new teeth growing up from the jaw

facts.statement: Qantassaurus ate plants such as ferns and horsetails, similar to its relative Leaellynasaura.
facts.quote: Like its close relative Leaellynasaura, its diet consisted of plants like ferns and horsetails

facts.statement: When Qantassaurus lived, Australia was part of the supercontinent Gondwana and lay partly within the Antarctic Circle.
facts.quote: At the time, Australia was part of the supercontinent of Gondwana, and partly within the Antarctic Circle

facts.statement: Scientists debate the average temperature of the region where Qantassaurus lived, with estimates ranging from -6 to over 5 degrees Celsius.
facts.quote: The average temperature of the region is contentious, with estimates ranging from -6 to well over 5 °C (21 to 37 °F)

facts.statement: Conditions in Qantassaurus's habitat were likely coldest during polar nights that lasted up to three months.
facts.quote: Conditions were likely to be at their coldest during the polar nights, which lasted up to three months

facts.statement: Evidence from related taxa suggests Qantassaurus was active year-round and did not hibernate.
facts.quote: Bone growth of presumed related taxa shows they were active all year round, so they did not hibernate through the winter

facts.statement: The bone structure of Qantassaurus suggests it was warm-blooded, which would help maintain body heat.
facts.quote: The structure of these bones also suggests warm-bloodedness, which would help maintain its body heat

facts.statement: Qantassaurus is classified as a basal iguanodont ornithopod.
facts.quote: Qantassaurus is a basal iguanodont ornithopod

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Qantassaurus was discovered on February 27, 1996.
facts.quote: The holotype of Qantassaurus was discovered on 27 February 1996

facts.statement: The holotype was found by Nicole Evered, a long-time participant in the excavation.
facts.quote: found by Nicole Evered, a long time participant of the dig

facts.statement: The fossils were found at Flat Rocks, an intertidal site near Inverloch in southeastern Victoria, Australia.
facts.quote: The dig occurred on the beach of the Bunurong Marine Park at the intertidal site known as Flat Rocks, near Inverloch, in southeastern Victoria, Australia

facts.statement: The species was named Qantassaurus intrepidus by Patricia and Tom Rich in 1999.
facts.quote: It was named Qantassaurus intrepidus by Patricia Vickers-Rich and Tom Rich in 1999

facts.statement: Qantassaurus was the size of a grey kangaroo and had large eye sockets that would help it see during polar nights.
facts.quote: Del tamaño de un canguro gris, tenía grandes cuencas oculares, que le ayudarían a ver durante la noche polar

facts.statement: It is suggested that Qantassaurus was a forager that grabbed ferns and other vegetation with its hands and ran from predators like a modern gazelle.
facts.quote: Qantassaurus probablemente era un buscador , que agarraba helechos y otra vegetación con sus manos y huía de los depredadores como una gacela moderna

facts.statement: The holotype of Qantassaurus was discovered on February 27, 1996, during the third annual field season of the Dinosaur Dreaming project.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Qantassaurus fue descubierto el 27 de febrero de 1996, durante la tercera temporada anual de campo del proyecto Dinosaur Dreaming

facts.statement: The excavation took place on the beach of Bunurong Marine Park at the intertidal site known as Flat Rocks, near Inverloch in southeastern Victoria, Australia.
facts.quote: La excavación ocurrió en la playa del Parque Marino Bunurong en el sitio intermareal conocido como Flat Rocks, cerca de Inverloch, en el sureste de Victoria, Australia.

facts.statement: Qantassaurus intrepidus was named by Patricia Vickers-Rich and Tom Rich in 1999.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado Qantassaurus intrepidus por Patricia Vickers-Rich y Tom Rich en 1999

facts.statement: The species name honors Queensland and Northern Territory Air Services, which transported fossils nationwide as part of the Great Russian Dinosaur Exhibition between 1993 and 1996.
facts.quote: en honor a los Servicios Aéreos de Queensland y el Territorio del Norte, que enviaron fósiles por todo el país como parte de la Gran Exhibición de Dinosaurios Rusos entre 1993 y 1996

facts.statement: The genus name Qantassaurus is an acronym, which is why a 'u' follows the 'q'.
facts.quote: QANTAS es un acrónimo , por lo que una u no sigue a la q en Qantassaurus

facts.statement: The specific name means "intrepid" in Latin, referring to the climatic challenges the small dinosaur faced.
facts.quote: El nombre específico significa "intrépido" en latín, en referencia a los desafíos climáticos que tuvo que enfrentar el pequeño dinosaurio.

facts.statement: Qantassaurus is a basal ornithopod that was originally assigned to Hypsilophodontidae in 1999.
facts.quote: Qantassaurus es un ornitópodo basal que fue asignado originalmente a Hypsilophodontidae en 1999.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodontidae is now understood to be an unnatural, paraphyletic group, and Qantassaurus was recovered recently as a basal iguanodontian by Boyd in 2015.
facts.quote: Hoy en día este se entiende que es un grupo no natural, es decir parafilético, y Qantassaurus fue recuperado recientemente como un iguanodontoniano basal por Boyd en 2015

facts.statement: It was more specifically recovered as a member of the iguanodontian clade Elasmaria by Rozadilla et al. in 2016 and Madzia et al. in 2017.
facts.quote: y más específicamente como miembro del clado iguanodontoniano Elasmaria por Rozadilla et al. en 2016 y Madzia et al. en 2017.

facts.statement: Qantassaurus lived 115 million years ago in Australia during the Late Aptian or Early Albian of the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Vivió hace 115 millones de años en Australia, durante el Aptiano tardío o Albiense temprano en el período Cretácico Inferior.

facts.statement: At that time, Antarctica was part of the supercontinent Gondwana and was located within the Antarctic Circle.
facts.quote: En ese tiempo, la Antártida era parte del supercontinente Gondwana, y se encontraba dentro del círculo antártico.

facts.statement: The average temperature ranged from -6°C to 3°C, and the polar night lasted up to 3 months.
facts.quote: La temperatura media se extendía desde los -6 °C a 3 °C y la noche polar duraba hasta 3 meses.

facts.statement: Bone growth demonstrates that hipsilophodontids were active year-round and did not hibernate during winter.
facts.quote: El crecimiento de los huesos demuestra que los hipsilofodóntidos estaban activos durante todo el año, así que no invernaban durante el invierno.

facts.statement: The bone structure of hipsilophodontids also suggests they may have been warm-blooded, which would help maintain body heat.
facts.quote: La estructura de los huesos de los hipsilofodóntidos también sugiere que pudieron haber sido de sangre caliente, lo que ayudaría a mantener el calor del cuerpo.

facts.statement: An astonishingly high number of Australian hipsilophodontid fossils show signs of disease, having been dragged and buried by melting ice at the end of winter.
facts.quote: Un número asombrosamente alto de fósiles australianos de hipsilofodóntidos muestran signos de enfermedad, que eran arrastrados y enterrados por el deshielo a finales del invierno.

facts.statement: Qantassaurus was likely a browser that cut ferns and other vegetation with its five-fingered hands and fled from predators like modern gazelles.
facts.quote: Qantassaurus era probablemente un ramoreador, que cortaba los helechos y otra vegetación con sus manos de cinco dedos y huía de sus depredadores como una gacelas modernas.

facts.statement: It may have had some form of defensive camouflage, such as spots or stripes.
facts.quote: Pudo haber tenido cierta clase de camuflaje defensivo, como manchas o rayas.

facts.statement: The time range for Qantassaurus is listed as Barremian to Barremian, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for Qantassaurus is Elasmaria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Elasmaria

facts.statement: Qantassaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: There are 2 fossil occurrences recorded for Qantassaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2

rejected.quote: One characteristic of the "Polar Victorian" euornithopods are distinctive spurs, or trochanters, on the upper surface of the thigh bone (or femur), where muscle was attached
